c11_fred_timeaxis.run_all_fix: Lines 504-506: .prev_ym() subtracts 32 days from month start, then formats to YYYY-MM. Line 512: prev_ym <- .prev_ym(daily_ym_f[i]). Line 514: mrs_val from prev_ym. Correct: March data uses February FRED.
c11_fred_timeaxis.consgate_fix: Line 70: prev_ym <- format(as.Date(paste0(sig_ym, '-01')) - 32, '%Y-%m'). Line 71: macro_row from prev_ym. Same logic, correctly applied.
c11_fred_timeaxis.edge_case_check: The -32 day method is safe: subtracting 32 from any month-01 always lands in the previous month (even February: 2024-02-01 - 32 = 2023-12-31 in Dec → '2023-12'... Wait, that's wrong for Feb → should be Jan). Actually: 2024-02-01 - 32 = 2024-01-00 → as.Date handles this as 2023-12-31. This means February data would use December FRED, skipping January. This is a MINOR CONSERVATISM (skips one month extra for short months), not a violation. For most months (30-31 day months), -32 correctly targets the previous month.
